selection.instruction: Revise the selected incumbent next; retain rejected candidate feedback as evidence.

rationale: The incumbent returned an empty list for every instance, which the diagnostics confirm as plan_semantics failures with goal_unsatisfied and zero executed actions. The spanner domain is a small, fully-observable STRIPS domain with deterministic effects and positive costs, so a plain breadth-first search over grounded actions guarantees a shortest legal plan whenever one exists within the step budget. I ground the three domain actions from the declared object types (man, location, spanner, nut), check preconditions against the current state, apply add/delete effects, and return the plan whose final state contains every goal tuple. Determinism is handled by sorting object names rather than relying on set iteration order, and inputs are never mutated.

rationale: The incumbent (planning-001) already solves all 10 observed instances with valid 10–13 step plans. Per the policy I may "finish early if all planning instances succeed", but I have remaining budget for a conservative tweak. Changes: (1) skip trivial self-walks (s==e) — they never appear in optimal plans but inflate the grounded action set; (2) raise max_steps from 900k to 1.5M and the per-node plan budget from 900 to 999 to remain robust on harder held-out spanner instances with more locations/spanners. State representation, grounding, and action formatting are unchanged so VAL-valid outputs are preserved. Prediction: total_successes should remain 10/10 (ceiling); I predict it stays at least at 10 (delta 0, expressed as increase with min_delta 0 to remain informative).
